facts.raw_span: a 2‐day history of right lower‐extremity numbness and pain
manual muscle testing of the right tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus was 3/5
gastrocnemius and flexor hallucis longus were 4/5
deep‐tendon reflexes were normal
Straight‐leg‐raising was positive at 70 degrees
the femoral‐nerve stretch test was negative
Plain radiographs showed degenerative scoliosis at L5–S1
Lumbar MRI demonstrated a right‐sided disc herniation at L5–S1
Initial peroneal‐nerve conduction studies revealed a motor conduction velocity of 51.5 m/s
Ankle‐brachial indices were decreased (0.78 on the right, 0.73 on the left)
lower‐extremity arteriography showed no significant vascular lesions
right foot drop (tibialis anterior, extensor hallucis longus, flexor hallucis longus, and peroneus longus 1/5; left side 4/5)

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of right lower-extremity numbness and pain, along with the findings of manual muscle testing and peroneal-nerve conduction studies, support this diagnosis.
The patient's positive straight-leg-raising test and the lumbar MRI findings of a right-sided disc herniation at L5-S1 support this diagnosis.
The patient's symptoms of numbness and pain, along with the findings of manual muscle testing and peroneal-nerve conduction studies, support this diagnosis.
The patient's decreased ankle-brachial indices and the development of foot drop support this diagnosis, although the lack of significant vascular lesions on arteriography makes it less likely.
The patient's plain radiographs showing degenerative scoliosis at L5-S1 support this diagnosis.
The lack of significant vascular lesions on lower-extremity arteriography and the progression of symptoms despite treatment for lumbar disc herniation suggest an alternative diagnosis.

rationales.F02: Muscle weakness in the right tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus suggests peroneal nerve palsy.
rationales.F05: Positive straight-leg-raising test suggests lumbar disc herniation.
rationales.F08: Lumbar MRI demonstrating a right-sided disc herniation at L5-S1 supports the diagnosis of lumbar disc herniation.
rationales.F09: Abnormal peroneal-nerve conduction studies support the diagnosis of peroneal nerve palsy.
rationales.F12: Right foot drop with muscle weakness in the tibialis anterior, extensor hallucis longus, flexor hallucis longus, and peroneus longus suggests peroneal nerve palsy.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including foot drop and weakness in the tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus, are consistent with peroneal nerve palsy, which is supported by the initial peroneal-nerve conduction studies and the absence of significant nerve-root or cord compression on MRI.
